status.en: 230 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 230 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to carry out lethal attacks across northern Nigeria, killing a Muslim cleric in northern Nigeria and multiple civilians in Plateau, including a 60‑year-old woman harvesting groundnuts. In eastern Nigeria gunmen killed at least ten people, and in the northeast a mass shooting in Binnari left dozens injured. Kidnappers abducted six residents in Kaduna's Millennium City estate and three vigilantes died in a separate Plateau incident. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å utføre dødelige angrep i Nord-Nigeria, og drepte en muslimsk prest i Nord-Nigeria og flere sivile i Plateau, inkludert en 60‑år gammel kvinne som høstet jordnøtter. I Øst-Nigeria drepte væpnede menn minst ti personer, og i nordøst ble det utført en masseskyting i Binnari som etterlot dusinvis sårede. Kidnapperne bortførte seks innbyggere i Kaduna-s Millennium City-område, og tre vakter døde i en separat hendelse i Plateau. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
